subject: mathematics
question_text: Prove that (cosh x − sinh x)ⁿ = cosh(nx) − sinh(nx).

mark_split.label: Simplify the right side and compare

verification.note: Source: Baby Bullet-Q, Junior Inter Maths-1A (Sri Publishers, Machilipatnam), book p.97 — VSAQ chapter 19 Hyperbolic Functions, answer 140.2. Printed appearances: TS 15 · AP 20. The twin of 140.1 with a minus. This time the eˣ terms cancel and the e⁻ˣ ones survive, so both sides collapse to e to the MINUS nx. ⚠ THE 1+1 SPLIT IS OURS, NOT THE BOOK'S — no [N Marks] tags are printed on these pages, which are set four questions to a page in two columns. recall_prompt: Say how you would do this one — name the formula or definition you use and how you finish.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Simplify the left side
steps.margin_note: First mark. With a minus between them the eˣ terms cancel instead, leaving e⁻ˣ — the mirror of the twin.

recall.must_convey: That cosh x − sinh x = e⁻ˣ because the eˣ terms cancel, so the left side is e⁻ⁿˣ.
accept: cosh minus sinh is e to the minus x because the positive exponentials cancel so the left side is e to the minus n x
this time the e to the x terms cancel leaving e to the minus x
the left side becomes e to the minus n x
cosh minus sinh ante e power minus x
the minus makes the other pair cancel
heard_as: e to the minus n x

steps.why: Which pair cancels depends on the sign between them. A plus kills the e⁻ˣ terms, a minus kills the eˣ ones — that is the entire difference between the twins.
common_mistakes: Copying the twin and writing eˣ.
Distributing the minus over only one term of the second bracket.

steps.label: Simplify the right side and compare
steps.margin_note: Second mark. The right side collapses the same way with nx, giving e⁻ⁿˣ, and the two agree.

recall.must_convey: That the right side also collapses to e⁻ⁿˣ, so both sides agree.
accept: the right side is also e to the minus n x so both sides agree
cosh n x minus sinh n x is e to the minus n x
both sides come to the same thing
right side kuda e power minus n x, rendu equal
from one and two they are equal
heard_as: e to the minus n x

steps.why: Taken together the twins say (cosh x ± sinh x)ⁿ = e^(±nx) — a compact fact worth carrying, since it makes both proofs immediate.
common_mistakes: Never stating that the two sides agree.
Losing the minus in the exponent.
